thread:
rina: Vendor just uploaded their commit+credit sheet. We need to translate into our cost model for Q3. Key things: phasing schedule, how credits cliff, and what % of capacity they expect to be preemptible. @tom @sara can you take?

vendor-bot: file uploaded: commit_credits_vendor_acme_q3.csv (s3://partner-uploads/acme/commit_credits_vendor_acme_q3.csv) :file_folder:

tom: grabbing it now. quick skim — they put a big upfront credit in month 1, then linear taper over 6 months. but the 'preemptible_mix' column is fuzzy (values like "low/med/hi"), not numeric.

sara: ugh. we need numeric proxies for the optimizer. propose mapping low=10%, med=30%, hi=60% unless partner gives explicit numbers. thoughts? :thinking_face:

eli: that mapping seems reasonable as a starting point. also need clarification on whether credits apply to reserved vs ephemeral usage differently. sheet looks like a single "credit_pool" column.

rina: good call. @maya from finance — will that mapping work for billing recognition? also: does an upfront credit change our effective committed revenue recognition for partner-backed reserved SKUs?

maya: short answer: we should treat partner credits as contra-revenue for the invoice period they apply to. If they are front-loaded we amortize across the credit window for P&L, but for our cost model we can expose both the gross rate and net-after-credit rate per month. mapping low/med/hi -> 10/30/60 is fine but flag as proxy.

tom: copying the header snippet here so we can script ingest: ```csv
vendor_sku,region,commit_tier,credit_pool_usd,phasing_months,preemptible_mix,apply_to_reserved_only
ACME-GPU-A,us-west,large,50000,6,med,false
```

eli: for the model we need deterministic numeric columns. I'll add a preprocessing step that: 1) maps preemptible_mix to numeric (per sara's proposal), 2) expands credit_pool_usd into monthly amortized credits per phasing_months, 3) marks whether credit only offsets reserved usage or all usage. I'll drop a transformed CSV back into the same bucket.

rina: also important: partner listed a latency premium for committed lanes (+5ms) in notes. that affects our routing cost decision (dedicated vs shared). can we capture that as a per-region latency delta in the model?

sara: we should. add a column `latency_premium_ms` during ingest. if partner doesn't specify, default to 0 and tag as unknown.

maya: for pricing conversations, finance wants to see two scenarios: (A) conservative: assume partner preemptible supply = mapped numeric, credits amortized as above; (B) aggressive: assume preemptible supply 20pp higher and credits usable across all usage immediately. will need monthly P&L impact for both.

tom: noted. I'll wire up the ingest and produce a small sample output (first 3 months) so we can sanity-check. quick example calc in the thread: if commit rate = $0.40/hr and partner credit = $50k over 6 months, and we expect 1000 reserved GPUs used evenly, net discount per-GPU-hour = (50000 / (6*30*24*1000)) ≈ $0.0116/hr.

eli: nice example — keep that per-GPU-hour calc in the scripts. also compute effective discount per-token for typical LLM footprints (e.g., 32k context, 0.02 tokens/sec baseline) so product can see unit economics.

sara: pinging @tom for ETA — can we have the transformed CSV + scenario A/B tables by EOD? I can start drafting the pricing note for the partner meeting.

tom: aiming EOD. I'll flag any rows with missing fields and call out assumptions in a README.

rina: thanks all. please tag me when the EOD artifacts are in s3 and paste the prescriptive mapping table in-thread. :slightly_smiling_face:

vendor-bot: committed file transformed and uploaded: commit_credits_vendor_acme_q3_transformed.csv (s3://partner-uploads/acme/commit_credits_vendor_acme_q3_transformed.csv)

tom: uploaded samples + scenario workbook to /shared/partnerships/acme/q3_scenarios.xlsx. last_message_ts=1769001456

maya: quick note — finance will need the amortized schedule in GL-friendly format (month, sku, gross_revenue_usd, credit_amortized_usd, net_revenue_usd). I'll review tomorrow.

rina: perfect. we'll iterate tomorrow after finance review. thanks everyone.
